listing.name: TimeSplitters 2 — Destinity13 native Linux recompilation
listing.summary: Prepare a native Linux player from your own USA PlayStation 2 disc image.
listing.download_block_reason: Portcove downloads are paused while the bundled compiler and first-start recovery are being reviewed. These steps cover an upstream copy you already trust and are permitted to use.

steps.title: Choose your original USA PlayStation 2 disc
steps.instruction: Use an ISO from your own TimeSplitters 2 USA disc, SLUS-20314. Setup checks SHA-1 01f074637a0328dd8e4ae62ac7564548e56ee126 for SLUS_203.14 inside the ISO. This check covers the game executable inside the disc.

steps.title: Keep the Linux x86-64 package together
steps.instruction: Extract TS2-Recomp-0.9.9-linux-x86_64.tar.xz into a writable folder. Use Python 3 and keep its tools, compiler and gs libraries together. The included graphics bridge requires glibc 2.34 or newer, libstdc++ with GLIBCXX_3.4.30 and the X11, udev, D-Bus, curl and zlib host libraries.

steps.title: Finish the upstream build
steps.instruction: Run TS2-Recomp.sh from its extracted folder and choose your ISO. Wait for both compilation passes and local graphics preparation. The launcher starts the resulting build/ts2/ps2EntryRunner_spiel with its data and library paths. If setup fails, check build/einrichten.log before retrying.

warnings: Keep the disc image, extracted game files and generated game code private. Retain the complete working copy before unpacking a newer release.
Use this route with a copy you already trust and are permitted to use. Maintain the package and generated player through upstream.

references.title: Keep saves and settings
references.instruction: Back up build/spielstand and the whole ts2-recomp folder under XDG_CONFIG_HOME, normally ~/.config/ts2-recomp. Keep your original ISO and the working folder that contains disc/inhalt, the generated build and any custom data.

references.title: Use the upstream Steam Deck launcher
references.instruction: Follow the upstream Steam Deck guide to complete the same build in Desktop Mode, then add TS2-SteamDeck.sh as a non-Steam game. Steam Deck behavior is documented by the upstream maintainer.
